title: every test pays for a real install even where the install is not what it tests: install once per file and copy it, amending D24
body:
## Problem

Every fixture goes through the real installer. `install_devbin` (tests/lib/test_helper.bash:305-330, at 9fedef14) runs `devbin install --into <dir> --force` for each one. That is design D24: a test-only installer could drift from the real one. An install costs 645 ms on this Mac.

dc profiled nine files: 694 tests, 50.6% of CI's suite time. Those files made 706 installs, 541 of them fixtures rather than installs that install.bats or localinstall.bats are testing. Installs took 34% of their time. Two files rebuild the same setup in every test:
- upgradeoffer.bats builds the same publish history each time (two installs and two upgrades, about 3.3 s) before the 1.2 s command it tests.
- releasecut.bats builds its project and remote each time, about 26 git calls (0.4 s).

Copying an installed fixture costs 12 ms with `cp -cR` (an APFS clone) or 32 ms with `cp -R`.

## Ruling

hv, 2026-10-08: install once per file and copy. This was dc's option 2, put to hv by vc, and it amends D24. D24's reason still holds: there is no second implementation of install, because every fixture is a copy of what the real installer wrote. The installer still runs at least once per file, and in every test of install.bats and localinstall.bats whose subject is the install.

## Fix

Each file installs its fixture once, through `install_devbin`, into a cache that no test writes, and each test copies it: `cp -cR` where the disk clones, `cp -R` elsewhere. Any other fixture a file builds the same way in every test is built once and copied the same way, including upgradeoffer.bats's publish history and releasecut.bats's project and remote. Whatever the installer writes outside the install directory is either in the copy or remade per test, so each test starts from the state a fresh install gives it today. D24's comment in test_helper.bash says what changed and cites this issue.

## Done when

1. Fixtures come from one real install per file and one copy per test, and there is no other route to an installed fixture.
2. No test can change what the next test copies, and the Resolution says what guards the cache.
3. Tests whose subject is the installer, or a fresh install's own state, still install per test. The Resolution names them.
4. The per-file build happens before a file's tests run, so it holds under `--jobs`, across files and within one.
5. The Resolution gives the profiled files' wall time on this Mac, before and after.

## Resolution

Landed at 96bc97d4 on a green full suite (vc's, 2352 of 2352 ok, 0 not ok, 5 skips, .errors empty, seal 20261016-1322 in ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-vc/land1016b/land/tmp/test/, 13:22:19Z to 13:32:35Z, on the stack tip 1dadcaa3 of ST0008 WP-02, 0199, 0192 and ST0008 WP-03).

- **Fixtures come from one real install per file and one copy per test (Done when 1).** setup_file runs the real installer once into a read-only cache, and install_devbin copies what an install writes, bin/devbin, bin/.devbin/lib/ and the manifest. doctor.bats's and scaffold.bats's fixtures, which need install's starter config, come the same way from one starter install per file, a project named demo declaring shell: 71 of their 72 uses. A copy is a real install, path, byte and mode, under umask 022 and 002, held by an arm.
- **No test can change what the next test copies (Done when 2), and what guards it is teardown_file.** Each cache is read-only to its owner, so a plain write fails where it is made; its sum, taken when it is built, is checked at teardown_file, which fails the file by name when a cache moved, is gone, or cannot be summed. A test that makes a cache writable first, or runs as root, gets past the modes, and only that check catches it.
- **The installer still runs per test where it is the subject (Done when 3):** install.bats and localinstall.bats; the publish and vendor calls from a source checkout in vendor, fleet, version, dispatch and upgradeoffer; doctor.bats's one fixture declaring no languages. It also runs where a fixture has no config yet, a bare directory, since install writes its starter there and a copy would not: the first landing suite found that one arm, shellinit.bats's machine-install fallback, red, and the fix is in the helper.
- **The caches are built in setup_file, before a file's tests run (Done when 4)**, so they hold under --jobs, across files and within one.
- **Time (Done when 5)**, the nine profiled files each run alone on this Mac, before and after, back to back under BSD: 1359.7s before and 993.9s after, 26.9% less, with every file all ok. The before half ran under higher load (1-minute load 4.2 to 25.0, against 3.5 to 11.0), so part of the difference is load. dispatch fell 57%, fullcycle 39%, doctor 33%, help 29% and releasecut 27%; localinstall and install, whose subject is the installer, moved little.

Declared:
- upgradeoffer.bats's publish history (about 3.3s a test, 21 tests) and releasecut.bats's project and remote (about 0.4s a test, 119 tests) are still built per test (vc's ruling): they carry each test's own directory in committed config, the machine pointer and the install's ancestry, so a copy would not be the state a fresh build gives; making them path-free would be its own issue;
- the cp -c probe runs under setup_file's PATH; no test puts another cp first before making a fixture.
- setup_file builds both caches in every file, including the 23 of 53 files that never install and the 51 that never use the starter shape, so every file pays two installs it may not use; the whole suite's wall, 10m16s (13:22:19Z to 13:32:35Z, 2352 tests in two lanes, 1-minute load 8.0 at its start), against 17m52s and 16m13s for the last two suites before 0192; the same stack's first run, red on the bare-directory fixture, took 11m49s at load 31, is the net figure beside the nine-file timing above.
